definitions.explanation: Woven or knitted material used for making clothing, curtains, and other items. Refers to the material itself, not a finished product.

examples.japanese: この{布地|ぬのじ}は{手触|てざわ}りがいい。
examples.english: This fabric feels nice to the touch.

examples.japanese: {高級|こうきゅう}な{布地|ぬのじ}を{使|つか}って{仕立|した}てたスーツは{着心地|きごこち}が{全|まった}く{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: A suit tailored from high-quality fabric feels completely different to wear.

notes:
Refers to textile material before it is made into a finished product. Composed of {布|ぬの} (cloth) + {地|じ} (base material/ground). Commonly used in sewing, fashion, and textile contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {布地|ぬのじ}を{裁|た}つ: to cut fabric
- {布地|ぬのじ}を{選|えら}ぶ: to choose fabric
- {綿|めん}の{布地|ぬのじ}: cotton fabric
- {絹|きぬ}の{布地|ぬのじ}: silk fabric
- {薄手|うすで}の{布地|ぬのじ}: thin/lightweight fabric

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {布|ぬの}: cloth — a more general and everyday word; can also refer to a finished piece of cloth
- {生地|きじ}: fabric, material — very similar to {布地|ぬのじ}; also means dough in cooking contexts
- {織物|おりもの}: woven fabric, textile — emphasizes the weaving process

USAGE:
{布地|ぬのじ} specifically refers to the raw material, while {布|ぬの} is broader. In everyday speech, {生地|きじ} is often used interchangeably with {布地|ぬのじ} for fabric.
